name: Charlie Black
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember surveying a legal boundary that no fence ever followed.” People around Tideline Market know Charlie by a small Sunday habit. Charlie picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I drew the boundary as a junior surveyor. This is the first time a client asked me how to make it friendlier.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a faded indigo overshirt and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Charlie has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Charlie looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Charlie is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To make the friendly boundary legal and clear.
family: Jo Wong is Charlie’s cousin. Charlie brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Jo makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Winter afloat*, Jo says, “I live in a flat above the coast road. I'm exchanging winter housing for summer sailing lessons I might be scared to take.”
connections: Stella Choi. The old childhood gap is a better starting point for the survey than the center of the hedge.

reactions.situation: The older neighbors disagree on where the gate should go
reactions.response: Charlie gets both neighbors to mark a trial gate position before any hedge is cut.
